read.reviewer: one evidence-reviewer agent (Claude Opus, effort max), read-only, no shell
read.scope: the merged signal handling and shutdown repairs of alert_probe.py, push_notification_probe.py, pty_probe_mutants.py, tmux_bell_probe.py and tmux_sync_probe.py, with their controls and the documents that describe them
read.why_not_a_gpt_read: the gateway pool's only usable account read 83 of 100 points and the other five read 100 until 2026-10-03/04, so a third GPT read would have taken the pool from the other sessions' running waves

findings.where: alert_probe.py and push_notification_probe.py, the exit path after a latched signal
findings.claim: A latched SIGINT became exit status 130 after the cleanups, a normal exit; a parent shell then runs its next command instead of stopping its loop after Ctrl-C.
findings.verification: shell_loop_control.py: bash went on for three runs after a child that exits 130 and stopped after a child that ends BY SIGINT (recorded/shell_loop_control.txt); Cracauer, cons.org/cracauer/sigint.html: the only way to report it is to kill yourself with the signal
findings.repair: end_by_latched_signal(): after the cleanups the probe resets the signal to its default action and sends it to itself; the signal cases expect the negative signal number; mutant 'a latched signal ends in an exit status instead of the signal'

findings.where: alert_probe.py and push_notification_probe.py, the spawn guard `if not stopped():`; pty_probe_mutants.py
findings.claim: No mutant and no case noticed the removal of the guard: with `if True:` the sweep still passed, although a client is then started after a stop request.
findings.verification: a mutated copy of alert_probe.py (`if True:`) passed sweep_case with '107 lines swept, the client was running at 15 of them, 0 problems'
findings.repair: the sweep records whether a stand-in client was ever started and fails when one was although the signal landed at or before the spawn guard; mutant 'the spawn is not guarded'

findings.where: the READMEs and the decision record ('a SIGTERM at EVERY line of the resource lifecycle'); sweep_case
findings.claim: The dry run stops at the trust dialog, so the sweep never reaches the lines after the prompt is typed, the observation loop, the report or the branches the dry run does not take.
findings.verification: v3 check on the merged files: 107 of 161 lines with code in main, with_private_dir and measure are swept for alert_probe.py (54 never) and 120 of 187 for push_notification_probe.py (67 never)
findings.repair: the sweep's detail now says how many lines it swept of how many lines with code; the READMEs and the decision record say what is and is not reached; the lines after the prompt is typed stay unswept

findings.where: the latch; 'first signal wins' in the documents
findings.claim: Signals that are pending together run their Python handlers in ascending signal number, so SIGHUP beats SIGINT beats SIGTERM whatever the sending order; 'first signal wins' holds one dispatch apart.
findings.verification: signal_order_probe.py: SIGTERM then SIGHUP ran as SIGHUP, SIGTERM; SIGTERM then SIGINT ran as SIGINT, SIGTERM (recorded/signal_order_probe.txt)
findings.repair: the latch docstring, the READMEs and the decision record say what 'first' means; no code change can recover the arrival order inside one dispatch

findings.where: with_private_dir, the installation of the latch
findings.claim: The latch replaced an inherited SIG_IGN (nohup, a background job), so a hangup aborted a run that was meant to ignore it.
findings.verification: by reading (the installation was unconditional) and by ignored_case, which fails on the old code
findings.repair: the latch is installed only for a signal whose disposition is not SIG_IGN; ignored_case; mutant 'an ignored signal is latched anyway'

findings.where: measure, the typing of the prompt
findings.claim: A stop request during the roughly 1.2 s of typing still sent Enter, so a model turn was submitted after the stop.
findings.verification: by reading (the typing loop and the Enter did not look at the latch)
findings.repair: type_prompt() checks the latch between keystrokes and before Enter; typing_case; mutant 'typing ignores the latch'

findings.claim: The false-pid control answers pid 1, so only the process-name check was exercised; the command-line clause of server_identity, the only one that refuses another tmux server, could be deleted with both controls green.
findings.verification: a copy of tmux_bell_probe.py without the clause ran its selftest: exit 0, '9 checks, 0 problems'
findings.repair: a third control answers the pid of another private tmux server, which must be left alone; the same mutation now ends with '9 checks, 1 problems' (recorded/tmux_identity_mutant_bell.txt and recorded/tmux_identity_mutant_sync.txt)

findings.where: the tmux probes, server_alive and the kill by pid
findings.claim: server_alive counted a zombie as alive; the check and the kill are not atomic (a pid reused inside the gap).
findings.repair: server_alive excludes state Z; pidfd_open with pidfd_send_signal would close the race and is not used

findings.claim: A subprocess timeout killed only the direct child and raised before the stand-in client was killed; in the mutant runner the TimeoutExpired aborted the run.
findings.repair: a timeout becomes a failed result and the stand-in is still killed through its pidfile; in the runner it is a failed case; a run killed from outside can still leave 'sleep 3137<digits>' processes (stated)

findings.where: the tmux probes, the pty.fork child
findings.claim: If the exec failed the child fell into the parent's code and its cleanup.
findings.repair: the child ends with os._exit(127) in a finally block

findings.claim: The README gave a count of BEL-counter cases that the code and the recorded selftest do not have.
findings.verification: by reading and by the recorded selftest output

verification_gaps: SIGHUP is covered by the in-process latch test only, not end to end
the tmux probes install no signal handler: a SIGTERM leaves the private server (until its pane exits) and its socket directory; nothing claims otherwise
the selftests exit 0 when end-to-end cases are skipped (no working directory, no tmux); only the mutant runner fails on a skip
the swept-line counts depend on the interpreter (the recorded output now names it)
